newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Riksbank chair criticises Swedish EMU view-paper.
newsitem.headline: Riksbank chair criticises Swedish EMU view-paper.

text.p: The chairman of Sweden's central bank said worries surrounding the Swedish crown could remain if the government does not take a stand on Europe's monetary union (EMU), a domestic weekly reported on Monday.
"There is no clear strategy," the weekly Veckans Affarer quoted Riksbank chairman Kjell-Olof Feldt as saying.
"As long as this prevails, we will have worries surrounding the crown."
The minority Social Democratic government has refrained from saying whether it is in favour of Sweden joining Europe's economic and monetary union.
It has said a party congress would make a decision this autumn, which is expected to be followed by a parliamentary ruling.

Feldt, which is a former Social Democratic Finance Minister, said it was clear that the lack of initiative regarding EMU has contributed to recent market volatility with climbing bond yields and a softening crown, Veckans Affarer said.
"The issue is not being dealt with at all," Feldt was quoted as saying. "This has probably led to investors thinking that Sweden won't participate. It is fairly clear that this has had an impact."
